newsitem.title: NORWAY: Lethargic Oslo shares dip, Orkla continues down.
newsitem.headline: Lethargic Oslo shares dip, Orkla continues down.

text.p: Norwegian shares ticked lower on Thursday in torpid activity, with few new impulses in the market.
Oslo's Total share index retreated 0.35 percent to close at 1,231.75 points. Dealers said the summer lull had clearly set in with turnover amounting to "a ridiculously low" 580 million crowns.

Food and beverage-based conglomerate Orkla spent a third consecutive session in negative territory and lost 12 crowns, or 2.1 percent, to end at 565 crowns in turnover of 42.4 million crowns. Orkla has lost 25 crowns since Tuesday.

The stock climbed strongly on Friday and Monday on market rumors that the group was near to sealing a production agreement with PepsiCo following the termination of Orkla's deal with Coca Cola Co. Orkla later denied the rumors.
Norway's largest bank Den norske Bank ASA (DnB) climbed 3.9 percent to 29.30 crowns in relatively heavy trade of 43 million crowns.

Dealers said the move was due to a positive analyst report in London. "Apparently there is a buy recommendation out in London and that's why there's so much buying interest," an Oslo based broker said.
